formula: If / When + Simple Present (V1 / V_s/es), Simple Present (V1 / V_s/es)
auxiliary: do / does (Negative/Interrogative mein); result mein 'will' nahi lagta
usage: Jab condition aur result ke beech automatic, 100% predictable, ya scientific cause-and-effect relationship ho. Ye timeless facts ke liye use hota hai.

patterns.affirmative: If water reaches 100°C under normal pressure, it boils rapidly.
patterns.negative: If an applicant does not sign the affidavit, the registry rejects the filing automatically.
patterns.interrogative: Does iron rust if you expose it to moisture and oxygen?

keyTip: EXAM TRAP: Result clause mein 'will' lagana galat hai ('it will boil' nahi). Permanent laws mein dono jagah strictly Simple Present hi lagta hai.

formula: If + Simple Present (V1 / V_s/es), Subject + will / shall + V1
auxiliary: will / shall in result clause; do / does in negative condition
usage: Aisi real aur possible situations ke liye jo future mein ho sakti hain, aur jinka result future mein hone ki high probability hoti hai.

patterns.affirmative: If the petitioner submits the surety bond tomorrow, the magistrate will issue the release order.
patterns.negative: If the clerk does not upload the digital roster, the lawyers will not attend the virtual court.
patterns.interrogative: Will the High Court stay the eviction if we file an urgent writ petition today?

keyTip: TEMPORAL CONSTRAINT: If-clause mein future auxiliary 'will' kabhi nahi lagta. 'If he will arrive, we will start' galat hai; 'If he arrives, we will start' sahi hai.

formula: If + Simple Present, can / may / must / should + V1 OR Imperative (V1)
usage: Jab result clause mein definite future result ki jagah ability, possibility, advice, ya direct administrative order dena ho.

patterns.affirmative: If the candidate clears the written test, he can sit for the Hindi typing examination.
patterns.negative: If you do not have a valid identity card, you cannot enter the court premises.
patterns.interrogative: If you witness tampering of evidence, report the matter to the bench immediately.

keyTip: IMPERATIVE TIP: Agar result clause mein subject na ho aur sidha order ya instruction ho, toh base verb V1 se sentence shuru karein (jaise 'If you need bail, contact the counsel').

formula: If + Simple Past (V2 / did + V1), Subject + would + V1
auxiliary: did in negative condition; would in result clause
usage: Present ya future ki aisi situation jo reality ke opposite hai, ya jiske hone ki possibility practical taur par bahut kam ya imaginary hai.

patterns.affirmative: If the clerk knew the root password of the database, he would fix the server glitch today.
patterns.negative: If the advocate did not have urgent hearings in Court No. 3, he would attend our conference.
patterns.interrogative: Would the judicial committee grant an extension if we requested more time?

keyTip: TIME DISTANCE RULE: Yahan 'Simple Past' beete huye kal ko nahi, balki reality se imaginary doori ko darshata hai. Isliye result clause mein 'would + V1' lagta hai.

formula: If + Subject (any person: I / he / she / it / they) + were ..., Subject + would + V1
auxiliary: were (formal subjunctive form for all persons)
usage: Contrary-to-fact present states aur hypothetical advice ('If I were you...') ke liye. Chahe subject singular ho ya plural, formal grammar mein 'were' lagta hai.

patterns.affirmative: If he were the Chief Registrar, he would modernize all court registries across Rajasthan.
patterns.negative: If the evidence were not so fragile, the forensics team would not preserve it in cold storage.
patterns.interrogative: If I were you, I would file an appeal against this interlocutory order immediately.

keyTip: TOP EXAM TRAP: Competitive exams mein 'If he was' distractor ke roop mein diya jata hai. Formal conditional syntax mein singular subjects ke sath bhi strictly 'were' hi choose karein.

formula: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + would have + V3
auxiliary: had in if-clause; would have in result clause
usage: Past ki aisi unfulfilled condition jo actually nahi hui, aur uska imagined past result jo ab kisi bhi tarah badla nahi ja sakta (past counterfactual/regret).

patterns.affirmative: If the prosecution had presented the forensic report, the magistrate would have convicted the accused.
patterns.negative: If the court clerk had not verified the records, the fraudulent decree would have been executed.
patterns.interrogative: Would the applicant have secured the job if he had scored two marks more in Part-B?

keyTip: FATAL CLAUSE CONFUSION: If-clause mein 'would have' lagana sabse badi galti hai ('If he would have studied' wrong!). If-clause mein strictly Past Perfect ('had + V3') lagta hai.

formula: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + could have / might have + V3
auxiliary: could have (past ability), might have (past possibility)
usage: Past unreal scenario mein definite outcome ki jagah past ability (kar sakta tha) ya past weaker possibility (shayad ho jata) express karne ke liye.

patterns.affirmative: If the fire brigade had arrived ten minutes earlier, they could have saved the record room.
patterns.negative: If the applicant had not forgotten his hall ticket, he might have cleared the written cutoff.
patterns.interrogative: Could the IT staff have recovered the corrupted files if they had maintained daily tape backups?

keyTip: MODAL SHADE: 'Would have' = definite hypothetical outcome; 'Could have' = ability was present; 'Might have' = speculative chance.

formula: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + would + V1 (now / today)
auxiliary: had in if-clause; would + V1 in result clause
usage: Jab past ke unfulfilled action ka asar current present moment par pad raha ho: Past Unreal Condition ➔ Present Result.

patterns.affirmative: If the system assistant had taken the networking certification last year, he would be a senior engineer today.
patterns.negative: If the court had not installed the solar plant in 2023, the electricity bills would be enormous now.
patterns.interrogative: If you had accepted the transfer last month, would you be working at the principal seat now?

keyTip: TIME ADVERB CLUE: Sentence mein past time marker ('last year') aur present time marker ('today/now') dono diye honge. Result mein 'would have been' nahi, 'would be' aayega!

formula: Had + S + V3... | Were + S + to + V1 / comp... | Should + S + V1...
usage: Formal English mein 'if' ko omit karke sentence ko inverted word order mein likha jata hai. Ye statements hoti hain, questions nahi.

patterns.affirmative: Had the registrar noticed the clerical error earlier, he would have recalled the order at once.
patterns.negative: Had the police not recorded the dying declaration, the case would have collapsed.
patterns.interrogative: Were the high court to order a judicial inquiry, the truth would come out.

keyTip: NEGATIVE INVERSION RULE: Negative sentence mein 'not' hamesha subject ke baad lagta hai: 'Had the witness not testified...' ('Had not the witness...' likhna severe error hai).

formula: Unless + Affirmative Clause (Simple Present), Result Clause (will not + V1)
auxiliary: do / does / will (subordinate clause mein 'not' prohibited hai)
usage: 'Unless' ka matlab hota hai 'if not'. Iske clause mein koi doosra negative word nahi aa sakta kyunki ye already negative hai.

patterns.affirmative: Unless the applicant submits the medical fitness certificate, the appointment will remain provisional.
patterns.negative: Unless the security team activates the firewall, unauthorized IP addresses will breach the database.
patterns.interrogative: Provided that the original vouchers are enclosed, the reimbursement claim will be sanctioned.

keyTip: DOUBLE NEGATIVE PROHIBITION: 'Unless you do not hurry' bilkul galat hai. Sahi construction hai: 'Unless you hurry, you will miss the hearing' (or 'If you do not hurry...').
